Choosing an unbleached coffee filter may be a small choice in the scheme of things, but it’s one that’s better for the environment and potentially you. These filters have not gone through the process involving chlorine and oxygen that bleaches the filters white. This means you don’t have to worry that these chemicals (however minuscule the amount) have entered your coffee and, thus, your body. What I notice about these filters is that they are not too thin, and the resulting coffee tastes no different from coffee made using bleached filters. The flat-bottomed filters, which look like cupcake liners, will fit most 8-12 cup coffee makers.

we purchased two of these based on the price and reviews. Sad to say but, we totally disagree with others reviews. The fit and shape of the filter was the same as the original GE MWF filter and the price was 1/3 of the GE. That is all I can say on the positive side. After installing and doing an initial flush to purge air and loose carbon particles from the dispenser line, we tasted the water. Yuck, it tasted like iodine. I ran an additional 3+ gallons of water through and then we re tasted the water. Yuck, it still tasted like iodine. I removed the Crystala filter and replaced it with the used but, not used up, GE filter, purged the line and tasted the water. It was clean, looked and tasted great! The flow rate is still good so I reset the filter condition light on the refrigerator and we will use order GE brand when we need to. Now, I just need to see if we can get a refund for these over rated sub quality GE knockoffs.
